title: Shamshi-Adad V
summary: King of Assyria, younger son and chosen successor of Shalmaneser III.
description: King of Assyria after Shalmaneser III. Griffith & White (Reply to Beckman, Part 2) say he spent his reign reconquering the lands east of the Euphrates and died unexpectedly in 811 BC. Person record added from Griffith & White’s Reply to Beckman (OSF project 5b64m) on 2026-11-13.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year.

standby.note: Standby placement only. Chronological Framework of Ancient History prints this BC/AD year on the death entry (811 BC). It is not a sort year. No Anno Mundi, regnal length, or Julian Period figure was converted to obtain it.

death.citation: Griffith & White, "A Reply to Beckman’s Defense of Thiele’s Chronology, Part 2: An Objectivist Answer to the Assyrian Synchronisms," OSF preprint v2.10 (2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/DT6GX, section “The Tell al-Rimah Stela”, p. 15
death.note: Died unexpectedly; his son Adad-Nirari III succeeded as a minor.
